assumptions: Agents utilize reinforcement learning mechanisms to acquire values.
Early environmental feedback disproportionately impacts the initial policy weights.
Stochasticity in environmental events is sufficient to create non-convergent trajectories.
definition.falsification: If identical agents show negligible divergence in value metrics across diverse stochastic environments, the hypothesis of path-dependent value acquisition is falsified.
definition.statement: Two identical autonomous agents subjected to distinct stochastic environments in their early development phases will develop divergent value systems due to the path-dependent nature of reinforcement learning-based preference acquisition.
definition.uncertainty: The magnitude of divergence is sensitive to the specific reinforcement learning architecture and the definition of 'identical starting conditions'.
